review.brief:
Review RM35-gateway-adopt-clock (roadmap RM35 tier 6, module internal/gateway) against the DIFF, not the whole module. This tier had TWO failed suite runs before going green — scrutinise the fixes, not just the original adoption.

(1) Module-boundary compliance per ai/architecture.md — gateway is the ONLY module allowed to produce HTML; it adds internal/clock and reads other modules through public interfaces only.
(2) Roadmap D1, the tier's central claim: the browser_tz cookie STILL WINS for a signed-in user. Only the FALLBACK moved from time.UTC to clock.Zone(). Verify in tz.go that every cookie-present path is untouched. A cookie path that now ignores the cookie is a BLOCKER.
(3) startOfDay delegates to clock.CalendarDay(t, time.UTC) — verify byte-identical by reading internal/clock/calendar.go yourself. Confirm supercharger.go's startOfMonth and tz.go's startOfDayIn are deliberately untouched (D-gw-2), and that startOfDayIn's documented DST limitation still stands.
(4) The four handlers.go time.Now() -> clock.Now() swaps: design.md D-gw-4 claims each is byte-identical because the result is consumed by .Sub() or round-tripped through pgtype.Timestamptz. VERIFY that claim at each of the four sites. Any site where the zone label survives into a stored or rendered value is a finding.
(5) THE FIXES — scrutinise hardest here. (a) D-gw-5/D-gw-6: browserTodayNoCookie() was added to history_test.go and 3 anchors repointed. Confirm ONLY the 3 sites that compare against a HANDLER-computed window moved, and that the ~21 sites passing their own today into buildHistoryView/dashboardFor correctly still use startOfDay. A test repointed that did NOT need it is a finding — it would mask a real frame bug. (b) D-gw-7: buildHistoryPresets' Active now compares formatted dates instead of instants. Verify the pre-existing claim independently with `git show main:internal/gateway/handlers/history.go`. Confirm the date comparison is correct for BOTH negative-offset (America/Bogota) and positive-offset (Europe/Madrid) zones — reason about it; do not run tests.
(6) Roadmap D6 — no NEW tests added. browserTodayNoCookie() is a helper, not a test; confirm no new Test* function appeared. Confirm no existing expected value was weakened or deleted to reach green — this is the key anti-gaming check given two red runs.
(7) Doc-pack conventions: ai/go-conventions.md's timezone rule, ai/htmx-conventions.md and ai/htmx-go-integration.md if any markup or fragment wiring changed, and the i18n rule (every user-facing string bilingual through i18n.T). CLAUDE.md's docs-track-structural-change: internal/gateway/AGENTS.md must name internal/clock, and no comment may still claim the fallback is UTC.
(8) Performance-Profile (read-heavy) — buildHistoryPresets now formats dates in a loop on the render path. Judge whether that is acceptable; say so either way.
(9) No database object created or changed. Any schema/migration touch is a BLOCKER — it never passed the owner's design gate.
(10) Scope honesty: D-gw-7 is a bug fix BEYOND MAG-20's literal scope, taken with the owner's explicit approval (roadmap D32) and recorded with the missing regression test in backlog entry 19. Confirm that record is accurate and complete.

Test provenance: go build ./..., go vet ./internal/gateway/..., gofmt, make i18n-guard, make ui-guard and openspec validate --strict were ASSISTANT-run and pass. The suite was run and reported passing by the OWNER, on the third attempt, after the two fixes above. Judge test QUALITY by reading them; do NOT run the suite.

findings.note: internal/gateway/handlers/history_test.go:1891 (TestDashboard_HistoryRegionInsideDashboardContent) exercises the real GET /ui/dashboard handler with NO browser_tz cookie (only a session cookie is set; dashboardEngine never adds browser_tz), so it hits browserToday(c)'s no-cookie fallback exactly like the 3 tests D-gw-5/D-gw-6 already fixed. But its expected value is still computed the OLD way: `yesterday := startOfDay(time.Now()).AddDate(0, 0, -1)` — UTC-midnight-based — while the handler's actual defaultHistoryHref(today) now derives `today` from clock.Zone() (America/Bogota, UTC-05) via the same fallback. UTC-calendar-day and Bogota-calendar-day coincide except during the 5-hour window 00:00-05:00 UTC (19:00-00:00 Bogota); this test will intermittently fail during that window, purely by CI-run-time luck, and did not fail in either of the owner's two red runs by chance of timing. This falsifies design.md D-gw-6's framing that exactly 3 handler-computed-window sites needed repointing to browserTodayNoCookie() — there is a 4th, and it was missed. Roadmap D6 requires repairing every test this tier's fallback change breaks; this one is not yet repaired. Fix: replace `startOfDay(time.Now()).AddDate(0, 0, -1)` at line 1891 with `browserTodayNoCookie().AddDate(0, 0, -1)`, matching the 3 already-fixed sites.

findings.note: The leader's own follow-up scan flagged TestDashboardHistoryFragment_LabelsRenderedAndVerticalOnlyForNarrowWindows (history_test.go:1752) and TestDashboardHistoryFragment_LabelsMatchViewModelVerbatim_NoLongDateFormat (history_test.go:1803) as safe. That judgement is WRONG for both — they are a 5th and 6th site of the same bug class, just manifesting as a spurious 400 instead of a wrong string. Both build end := startOfDay(time.Now()).AddDate(0, 0, -1) (UTC-yesterday, Location=UTC) and pass it as an explicit ?end= query param with NO browser_tz cookie (historyEngine's /_session route sets only uid, never browser_tz). Server-side, DashboardHistoryFragment resolves today := browserToday(c) via the same no-cookie fallback, now clock.Zone() (Bogota) — so parseHistoryRange's cap computes yesterday := today.AddDate(0,0,-1) with Location=Bogota. calendarDateAfter(e, yesterday) compares e.Date() and yesterday.Date() using EACH time.Time's OWN Location (Go's Time.Date() semantics), not a common frame. Concrete counterexample at real time 2026-08-16T02:00:00Z: UTC-yesterday's calendar date is 2026-08-15 (UTC), but Bogota-yesterday's calendar date is 2026-08-14 (Bogota is still on the 15th as 'today' at that instant). calendarDateAfter(2026-08-15, 2026-08-14) = true, so parseHistoryRange rejects the request as 'end after browser-yesterday' -> ok=false -> the handler returns HTTP 400. Both tests assert 200 (`t.Fatalf("want 200, got %d", w.Code)`) and will fail with a 400 during the same 00:00-05:00 UTC / 19:00-00:00 Bogota window R1-1 already identified. This is not a hypothetical: it is the identical frame-mismatch mechanism, just tripping the validation cap instead of a string comparison. The leader's stated reasoning ('end is UTC-yesterday and today is Bogota-today, so it clears the cap in either frame') does not hold once the two Locations are compared through calendarDateAfter's own-Location semantics. Fix: in both tests, replace `end := startOfDay(time.Now()).AddDate(0, 0, -1)` with `end := browserTodayNoCookie().AddDate(0, 0, -1)`, mirroring R1-1's fix -- this makes the calendar-date STRING placed in the URL agree with the handler's own Bogota-frame yesterday, so calendarDateAfter always compares equal calendar dates regardless of which 5-hour window the suite runs in.

decisions.decision: startOfDay is kept as a one-line named wrapper over clock.CalendarDay rather than deleted at its call sites.
decisions.why: Unlike telemetry's dateOnly, the name carries meaning at gateway call sites. Deleting it would churn more lines than it saves.

decisions.decision: startOfDayIn is left byte-identical; only a cross-reference comment is added.
decisions.why: It is a zone-parameterised helper with a documented DST limitation, not a duplicated UTC truncator. The roadmap row lists it as a deliberate keep.

decisions.decision: browserToday's own time.Now() is NOT swapped for clock.Now().
decisions.why: The roadmap row does not list it, and the swap would be a no-op — the value is immediately re-converted into the browser's own zone.

decisions.decision: All four handlers.go swaps are asserted byte-identical rather than behaviour-changing.
decisions.why: Each result is either consumed by .Sub() or round-tripped through pgtype.Timestamptz, both of which discard the zone label.

decisions.decision: The 3 tests are repaired to anchor on the handler's own fallback; the Bogota fallback itself is NOT reverted.
decisions.why: A cookie-carrying user already got a -05 window before this tier. T1 only changed the no-cookie default, which is exactly what roadmap D1 asked for. The tests asserted the old default.

decisions.decision: A named helper browserTodayNoCookie() is added rather than inlining startOfDayIn(time.Now(), clock.Zone()) at each of the 3 sites.
decisions.why: 21 other sites correctly keep startOfDay. The helper's doc comment records which anchor belongs where, so the next edit cannot silently pick the wrong one.

decisions.decision: Fix the pre-existing buildHistoryPresets instant-vs-date comparison inside tier 6 rather than as a separate change or by reverting the tier.
decisions.why: Owner chose it from three options. The test cannot go green without either this fix or a weakened assertion, and weakening is forbidden.

decisions.decision: R1-1 accepted in full — no triage pushback.
decisions.why: Verified independently: the test drives the real handler with no cookie and formats a UTC-derived date. It fails only 00:00-05:00 UTC, which is why three suite runs passed it.

decisions.decision: R2-1 accepted in full; the leader's round-1 'both safe' judgement is recorded as WRONG rather than quietly dropped.
decisions.why: Leader misread parseHistoryRange's cap as end<=today. It is end<=yesterday, and calendarDateAfter compares each time in its own Location. The reviewer's worked example is correct.

decisions.decision: Two distinct test anchors: browserTodayNoCookie for the both-params-absent path, browserYesterdayUTC for the explicit ?start=&end= path.
decisions.why: parseHistoryRange returns browser-zone midnight for the default window but UTC midnight from time.Parse for explicit params. One anchor cannot serve both.
